## **2\. Product Background**

In secondary and higher education, history has long been perceived by many students as a dry and challenging subject. Traditional approaches predominantly rely on rote learning-compelling learners to passively memorize chronological dates, landmark treaties, and isolated historical figures to prepare for examinations. This conventional model suffers from a significant deficit in contextual immersion and interactivity, which rapidly leads to student disengagement and superficial knowledge retention. Once examinations conclude, most factual historical details are quickly forgotten because students were never afforded the opportunity to interact actively with historical events or analyze motives through multiple perspectives. 

Concurrently, educational institutions, secondary schools, and history educators face noticeable infrastructural limitations. In the contemporary digital education landscape, schools and teachers lack dedicated, domain-specific EdTech platforms tailored to history education. General-purpose learning management systems (LMS) do not offer integrated historical knowledge bases, interactive geographical battle maps, or convenient transferring of localized historical contexts to classrooms. Teachers spend excessive manual effort assigning supplementary reading materials, grading standardized quizzes, and attempting to monitor whether students genuinely comprehend the underlying historical causality during self-study sessions.

To overcome these dual educational bottlenecks, the student development team, under the mentorship of Lecturer Huỳnh Công Việt Ngữ, initiated the HistoryTalk project. HistoryTalk is designed as an advanced Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) educational platform operating concurrently across B2C (individual self-directed learners) and B2B (schools, teachers, and classrooms) segments. By combining Conversational AI with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) anchored in authenticated historical archives, HistoryTalk mitigates the risk of artificial intelligence hallucination while delivering an engaging, interactive, and academically verified learning journey. Simultaneously, its cloud-native SaaS architecture provides an all-in-one platform for schools, teachers, and students-combining interactive, verified learning with centralized tools for classroom management, content distribution, and student progress tracking without any local infrastructure barriers. 

## **3\. Existing Systems**

To formulate the system architecture and feature set of HistoryTalk, the development team performed a comprehensive comparative analysis of existing commercial and educational systems, evaluating both their distinctive strengths and their inherent architectural limitations.

### **3.1 Character.AI**

Character.AI (https\://character.ai) is a prominent generative artificial intelligence platform utilizing large language models (LLMs) to simulate conversational interactions with user-created virtual personas, including celebrities, fictional figures, and historical personalities.

* **Key Features:** Natural language persona configuration, open-ended multi-turn dialogue, community-driven persona sharing, and voice synthesis.  
* **Pros:** Delivers highly engaging, expressive, and naturalistic conversational dialogues with diverse characters; offers high user retention through customizable personality prompts.  
* **Cons:**  
  * High vulnerability to factual hallucination (AI fabricating dates, historical events, and false facts), complete absence of grounded academic knowledge retrieval (no verified RAG)  
  * It lacks safety rules and educational filters to ensure accurate, classroom-appropriate responses.  
  * It does not support school curriculums, tests, quizzes, or tools for teachers and schools to manage students.

### **3.2 Google Classroom**

Google Classroom ( https\://classroom.google.com) is a widely adopted web-based learning management system (LMS) developed by Google to simplify creating, distributing, and grading educational assignments paperlessly.

* **Key Features:** Class roster creation, assignment distribution, deadline reminders, Google Drive/Docs integration, and grade tracking.  
* **Pros:** user management; clean teacher-student workflow; reliable assignment submission and grade recording.  
* **Cons:**  
  * Acts merely as a repository for static documents and links; offers no interactive storytelling, historical reenactment, or engaged learning.  
  * Cannot simulate discussions with historical figures or provide interactive tutoring when students study independently.  
  * Completely lacks interactive historical maps, chronological battle timelines and history knowledge bases.

## **4\. Business Opportunity**

The global and domestic educational technology (EdTech) market is currently undergoing a profound paradigm shift, spurred by breakthroughs in Generative Artificial Intelligence and the rising demand for personalized, active learning environments. In the domain of humanities and history education, a significant commercial and pedagogical gap remains unaddressed: traditional digital products remain purely static repositories of scanned texts and recorded videos, whereas modern generic AI chatbots (e.g., standard ChatGPT or unconstrained LLMs) are inherently prone to hallucinations, rendering them unsuitable and untrustworthy for formal academic deployment.

HistoryTalk bridges this market void by establishing an end-to-end historical learning ecosystem that integrates verified domain knowledge with high-immersion conversational engagement, addressing two lucrative market segments:

1. **Consumer Market (B2C):** For individual students, lifelong history enthusiasts, and parents seeking effective supplementary learning tools, HistoryTalk provides an interactive four-stage learning journey: (1) exploring core historical event overviews and historical videos, (2) conversing directly with AI-driven historical personas, (3) navigating historical battles and landmarks on interactive maps, and (4) taking self-evaluation quizzes. A tiered subscription model (Free, Plus, Pro) integrated with seamless PayOS payment allows flexible, self-service user monetization.  
2. **Institutional Market (B2B):** For secondary schools, high schools, and educational centers undergoing digital transformation, HistoryTalk operates as a multi-tenant SaaS platform. School Administrators and Teachers can manage digital classrooms, assign curriculum-aligned historical contexts, create localized historical characters and quizzes (tailored to provincial or institutional heritage), and monitor students regarding quiz scores and AI conversational frequency.

By grounding its conversational LLM in authenticated historical archives via Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) with verified historical documents, HistoryTalk establishes educational credibility and eliminates the hallucination barrier. This unique value proposition firmly aligns with national educational directives prioritizing digital competency, active student engagement, and institutional management.

## **5\. Software Product Vision**

For secondary and high school students, history enthusiasts, and educational institutions who seek an engaging, immersive, and systematically method to learn and teach history, the HistoryTalk Platform is a cloud-based, multi-tier educational SaaS web application that combines RAG-powered Conversational AI roleplay, interactive historical maps, multimedia exploration, and comprehensive classroom management. Unlike traditional static e-learning websites and ungrounded public conversational bots, our product guarantees historical factual accuracy through verified knowledge base retrieval, provides an immersive first-person dialogue with historical figures, and equips educators with tools to manage and track student comprehension and curriculum mastery.

## **6\. Project Scope & Limitations**

The project scope defines the functional boundaries of the HistoryTalk platform for the Capstone Project. It details the core feature modules delivered during development and identifies project limitations to set clear expectations.

### **6.1 Major Features**

**FE-01:**	**Authentication & Authorization (Module 1):** User registration and login via Email/Password, with integrated Google Login. Includes an individual user flow supporting account upgrades to Premium packages (B2C), and a SaaS institutional flow where System Admins create School Admin accounts, and School Admins manage Teacher and Student accounts (B2B).

**FE-02:**	**Classroom Management (Module 2):** Dedicated school management system. School Admins can create, edit, delete, and view school-wide classrooms. Teachers can add or remove students in their classes, assign learning tasks (historical contexts, character conversations, and quizzes), and create localized content and regional history quizzes visible only to their classes.

**FE-03:**	**Learning & Interaction (Module 3):** Displays historical events, historical character profiles, and lesson videos. Provides interactive Conversational AI where students chat via text and voice with AI historical figures (powered by RAG to prevent hallucinations). Includes an Interactive Map showing geographical landmarks and battlefields, along with practice quizzes and graded tests.

**FE-04:**	**Daily Token Management (Module 4):** Manages daily token balances for individual Customers and School Students. Automatically restricts chat access when tokens are exhausted and displays upgrade suggestions. Replenishes daily tokens upon daily login.

**FE-05:**	**Progress Tracking & Analytics (Module 5):** Allows students to view quiz history and assigned task progress. Provides teachers with classroom dashboards to monitor student quiz scores and track AI interaction engagement (number of messages exchanged with AI characters).Manages Premium subscription tiers, integrates the PayOS online payment gateway, and records transaction history and subscription status.

**FE-06:**	**Individual Online Payment (Module 6):** Service portal for individual learners to purchase subscription packages, integrated with the PayOS payment gateway, featuring transaction history logging and subscription status tracking.

**FE-07:**	**System Content Management (Module 7):** Administrative portal for Content Admins to manage the academic database, including historical events, character personas, documents/knowledge base, and quiz question banks, with content publish/inactive status control.

**FE-08:**	**Mobile App (Module 8):** Product roadmap and architectural design to develop cross-platform mobile access, optimizing on-the-go learning for both individual customers and school students.

**Figure 6-1. Major Features Mindmap of HistoryTalk Platform**

### **6.2 Limitations & Exclusions**

**LI-01:**	**Geographical and Curricular Scope:** The initial implementation and curated knowledge base of HistoryTalk are strictly focused on major historical battles in Vietnamese National History. Other general historical topics and world history are excluded from the current Capstone scope.

**LI-02:**	**Platform Deployment Boundary:** The platform is currently developed and deployed as a responsive Web Application and an Android mobile application. An iOS application is not supported in this initial release and is planned for future updates.

**LI-03:**	**AI Guardrails and Domain Confinement:** The Conversational AI agent is strictly bounded by prompt engineering guardrails and verified knowledge retrieval. The AI is programmed to reject out-of-domain conversational topics, modern geopolitical debates, controversial speculative history, and sensitive unverified claims.

**LI-04:**	**Domestic Payment Method Confinement:** The PayOS payment gateway is implemented for B2C individual subscriptions via Vietnamese domestic banking. B2B institutional payments and international payment gateways (e.g., PayPal, Stripe) are not supported in this release.

### **1.2 Project Objectives**

The project aims to develop HistoryTalk, an interactive historical education platform powered by Conversational AI and RAG Technology. The system connects secondary and high school students with historical figures through first-person roleplay dialogue, while equipping educators with a comprehensive classroom assignment workflow.

1. **Target Metrics**  
   1. **Quality**  
      1. **Test Coverage:** Achieve a minimum of 85% coverage for core service and AI RAG modules.  
      2. **Defect Rate:** 0 Critical/Blocker defects, and below 5 minor defects during the UAT phase.  
   2. **Time**  
      1. Complete the Capstone Project on time from September 2026 to December 2026 across 15 weeks.  
      2. Adhere to an iterative Agile development process with 2-week sprints.

| \# | Testing Stage | Test Coverage | Target No. of Defects | % of Defect | Notes |

| 2 | Unit Test | \>=80% | \< 5 Minor | 30% | Core service logic, Flyway migrations, and AI RAG semantic search. |
| 3 | Integration Test | \>=85% | \< 3 Medium | 20% | REST API communication between Java Spring Boot Backend and Python AI Service. |
| 4 | System Test (E2E) | 100% Flows | 0 Blocker | 20% | End-to-end student AI roleplay, quiz submission, and educator gradebook workflows. |

### **1.3 Project Risks**

| \# | Risk Description | Impact | Possibility | Response Plans |
| ----- | :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | LLM Hallucination Risk: Generative AI invents inaccurate historical facts or dates during roleplay. | High | Medium | Implement two-step RAG (Dense retrieval \+ Rerank) and strict system prompts. |
| 2 | Student Chat Spamming: Students submit random characters to trick the assignment message counter. | Medium | High | Set minimum character length filter (\>= 10 chars) and deduct user tokens per chat message/character length to prevent spamming, while anchoring final grades to timed Quiz assessments. |
| 3 | PayOS Webhook Failure: Payment notification dropped during network instability leading to missing token credit. | High | Low | Implement background reconciliation scheduler (PaymentFulfillmentReconciliationScheduler) for polling. |
| 4 | OCR Processing Failures: Scanned historical PDF documents with low DPI or noise fail OCR extraction. | Medium | Low | Configure Tess4J preprocessing with DPI enhancement (300 DPI) and PDFBox text fallback. |

## **2\. Management Approach**

### **2.1 Project Process**

The team applies the Agile Scrum software development model across 15 weeks.

1. The project is managed through iterative and incremental software releases.  
2. Short 2-week Sprint cycles allow for continuous requirement refinement, weekly supervisor feedback, and seamless service integration.

### **2.2 Quality Management**

The approach to quality assurance is based on non-functional requirements and testing processes:

2. **Reviewing:** Conduct mandatory peer review of pull requests among team members before merging into staging/main.  
3. **Automated Testing & CI/CD:** Automated build and test validation via GitHub Actions, building Docker images to GHCR and auto-deploying to AWS EC2.  
4. **Performance Testing:** Test SSE streaming latency (Time-To-First-Token \< 2s) and API throughput under concurrent classroom sessions.  
5. **Academic Integrity Check:** Enforce anti-spam message filters (\>= 10 chars), character-length token deduction rules, and timed Quiz sessions as the primary evaluation anchor.

# **III. Software Requirements Specification** {#iii.-software-requirements-specification}

## **1\. Overall Description** {#1.-overall-description}

### **1.1 Product Overview** {#1.1-product-overview}

HistoryTalk is a Software-as-a-Service platform for Vietnamese history education. It replaces passive memorization with interactive learning: learners talk with AI-simulated historical figures whose answers are grounded in curated documents, explore events on a time-based map, and check their knowledge with quizzes.

The platform serves two business models:

1. **B2C (individual learners):** a Customer registers for free (Free tier) and may buy the Plus or Pro package via PayOS VietQR to receive more AI tokens.  
2. **B2B (secondary and high schools):** each school is an isolated tenant with an annual enterprise package (01/09 – 31/05) that provides a shared token pool. The School Admin imports students, manages classes and teachers and sets daily token limits. Teachers create local historical content and assign homework (read a context, chat with a character, or take a quiz) to their classes and track results.

![][image3] 

| External Entity | Interaction with HistoryTalk |
| :---- | :---- |
| PayOS Gateway | Creates payment links with VietQR, sends signed payment webhooks, answers order queries. |
| AI Service (FastAPI) \+ LLM provider (Ollama or OpenAI-compatible API) \+ re-ranker | Receives grounded prompts, streams answers with token usage; chunks and embeds documents. |
| Google Identity | Verifies Google ID tokens for sign-in. |
| Email Service (SMTP) | Delivers password-reset links and temporary passwords for Google-created accounts. |
| Supabase Storage | Stores avatars, character/context media, map images and uploaded PDFs; files are served by time-limited signed URLs. |

**Scope**

* **In scope (Release 1.0):** web application for all six roles; AI character chat; historical map; quizzes and question bank; gamification; school tenant lifecycle; classroom, student and teacher management; assignments; local content; token tickets; B2C payment via PayOS VietQR; content curation with PDF extraction and OCR.  
* **Out of scope:** native mobile app; payments other than PayOS VietQR; online B2B invoicing (school contracts are billed offline and recorded by the System Admin); teacher-to-student messaging; UI languages other than Vietnamese.

**Assumptions & Dependencies**

* PayOS, Google Identity, the LLM provider and Supabase are third-party services; their outage only degrades the related functions (REL-04).  
* AI latency targets assume the LLM provider meets its own published latency.  
* Each school provides unique student codes in its roster file.

**Definitions & Acronyms**

| Term | Definition |
| :---- | :---- |
| Tenant | A school registered on the platform; its data is isolated from other schools. |
| Learner | A Customer or a School Student. |
| Historical Context | A historical period or event (e.g., "Chiến dịch Điện Biên Phủ 1954") used to group characters, documents, quizzes and map data. |
| Global content | Content curated by Content Admins (no school), visible to everyone when published. |
| Local content | Content created by a Teacher for his/her school (scope CLASS\_ONLY or SCHOOL\_WIDE). |
| Token | Unit of AI usage; one chat turn costs the total model tokens reported by the AI service (BR-08). |
| School pool | The school's remaining token quota (unallocatedTokenQuota), shared by all its students and teachers. |
| Token ticket | A request for extra daily tokens (TokenBoostRequest). |
| RAG | Retrieval-Augmented Generation. |
| SSE | Server-Sent Events, used to stream AI answers. |
| OCR | Optical Character Recognition (Tess4J, Vietnamese language data). |

* **Tenant, accounts & sessions:** BR-01 – BR-07.  
* **Token economy:** BR-08 – BR-12.

* **Content & AI grounding:** BR-16 – BR-19.

## **2\. User Requirements** {#2.-user-requirements}

### **2.1 Actors** {#2.1-actors}

| \# | Actor | Description |
| ----- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | Customer | Individual (B2C) user. Registers by email or Google, holds a token balance, chats with characters, explores the map, takes quizzes, buys packages. |
| 2 | School Admin | Administrator of one school. Imports students, manages classes, teachers and students, sets token policy, moderates local content, reviews token tickets, rolls over the academic year. |
| 3 | Teacher | Instructor of a school, homeroom teacher of one or more classes. Creates local content and assignments for own classes, monitors results, approves student token requests from his/her daily allowance. |
| 4 | School Student | Student belonging to a school tenant. Logs in with school-issued credentials, does assignments, chats within the daily limit, requests extra tokens. Cannot purchase packages. |
| 5 | Content Admin | Platform history specialist. Curates global contexts, characters, documents, quizzes, question bank, map data, daily quests and trash. |
| 6 | System Admin | Platform super-administrator. Provisions schools and School Admins, manages school subscriptions, user accounts and tiers, monitors dashboards. Has all Content Admin rights. |
| 7 | PayOS Gateway | External payment system that processes VietQR transfers and sends payment webhooks. |
| 8 | AI Service | External FastAPI service \+ LLM \+ re-ranker that generates grounded answers and document embeddings. |
| 9 | Google Identity | External identity provider used for Google sign-in. |
| 10 | Email Service | External SMTP service that sends system emails. |

"Learner" is used in diagrams as a generalization of Customer and School Student.

#### ***3.1.4 Non-Screen Functions***

| \# | Feature | System Function | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | AI Chat  | AI Answer Streaming & Token Deduction | Builds the grounded prompt, streams the answer via SSE, saves the messages and deducts tokens (3.4.3). |
| 2 | Token | Daily Allowance Preparation (lazy reset) | On the first chat of a new day, resets a school user's daily used/bonus counters and computes the available tokens (3.4.4). |
| 3 | Payment  | Payment Webhook Handler | Receives PayOS webhooks, verifies the signature and completes the order (3.8.3). |
| 4 | Payment | Payment Order Expiry Job | Every 60 s: PENDING orders past expiredAt become EXPIRED (3.8.4). |
| 5 | Payment | Subscription Expiry Job | Every 5 min: paid user tiers past endTime become inactive (3.8.4). |
| 6 | Payment | Payment Fulfillment Reconciliation Job | Every 60 s: retries fulfillment of PAID orders whose fulfillment is PENDING or FAILED (3.8.4). |
| 7 | Content | Document Extraction & OCR | Extracts text from PDFs with PDFBox; scanned pages are processed by Tess4J OCR (Vietnamese, 300 dpi) with streamed progress (3.11.3). |
| 8 | Content | Document Indexing (AI Service) | Splits document text into semantic chunks, embeds them and stores them in vector\_chunk (3.11.3). |
| 9 | School | School Subscription Guard | On each request of a school user, rejects access when the school is EXPIRED/SUSPENDED/INACTIVE or outside the subscription dates (BR-13). |
| 10 | Token | Customer Daily Token Allowance (lazy grant) | On a Customer's first sign-in or chat of a new day, adds the daily token amount of the active tier (Free, Plus or Pro) to the balance; unused tokens accumulate (3.4.5). |

#### ***3.1.5 Entity Relationship Diagram***

Attribute-level design (data types, keys, indexes) is defined in Report 4 – Software Design Description.  
**![][image16]**   
**Entities Description**

| \# | Entity | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1 | User | Account of any of the six roles: username, email, BCrypt password, profile, role, school, student code, mustChangePassword, account status (ACTIVE/DEACTIVATED), token balance, daily used/bonus tokens, last reset time, password-reset token hash and expiry, soft-delete time. |
| 2 | School | Tenant: name, unique school code, contacts, enterprise package, total and remaining token pool, subscription start/end, renewal flag and next package, default daily student/teacher quota, local-history policy accepted, status (ACTIVE/INACTIVE/SUSPENDED/EXPIRED). |
| 3 | Classroom | Class of a school: name, code, grade level, academic year, homeroom teacher, daily token quota, status (ACTIVE/ARCHIVED). |
| 4 | Class Student | Enrollment of a student in a class with join time and status. |
| 5 | Token Boost Request | Token ticket: school, class, student, requester and role, requested/approved tokens, reason, status (PENDING/PENDING\_ADMIN/APPROVED/REJECTED), teacher and admin review data. |
| 6 | Class Local Content | Assignment of a local context/character to a class. |
| 7 | Tier | B2C package: title (free/plus/pro), amount (VND), number of months, token amount, daily token amount, active flag. |
| 8 | User Tier | A user's subscription: tier, payment order, start/end time, active flag. |
| 9 | Payment Order | Purchase: order code, amount, description (transfer content), tier, status (PENDING/PAID/CANCELLED/EXPIRED/FAILED), fulfillment status (PENDING/PROCESSING/FULFILLED/FAILED), expiry time. |
| 10 | Payment Transaction | PayOS transaction data received for an order (status PENDING/SUCCESS/FAILED). |
| 11 | Daily Check-In | One check-in of a user per day with streak count. |
| 12 | Daily Quest | Quest definition: type (CHAT/QUIZ/READ\_CONTEXT), title, target, reward tokens. |
| 13 | User Quest Progress | A user's daily progress and claimed flag for a quest. |
| 14 | Historical Context | Period/event: name, description, era, category, year range, BC flag, location, image, video, battle map, coordinates, published flag, school (null \= global), scope (CLASS\_ONLY/SCHOOL\_WIDE), content status, review note, approver, soft-delete time. |
| 15 | Character | Historical figure: name, title, background, personality, image, 3D model URL, birth/death dates (with BC flags), published flag, contexts, school and content status for local characters. |
| 16 | Document | Reference source of a context or character: title, type (TEXT/MARKDOWN/PDF), content, file path, status. |
| 17 | Document Media Metadata | Media attached to a document/entity (e.g., video). |
| 18 | Vector Chunk | A passage of a document with its embedding (stored by the AI service in pgvector). |
| 19 | Map Pin | Point on the map of a context: label, description, pin type, owner type, coordinates, year, path GeoJSON. |
| 20 | Map Focus | Ordered camera focus of a context's map story: name, description, center, zoom level, order, default/active flags. |
| 21 | Chat Session | Conversation between a user and a character (optionally linked to a local scenario). |
| 22 | Message | One user question or AI answer: content, message type, token count, suggested questions, quotes. |
| 23 | Quiz | Set of questions of a context: title, level (EASY/MEDIUM/HARD), published flag, creator, soft-delete time. |
| 24 | Question | Bank question: content, explanation, type (MULTIPLE\_CHOICE/FILL\_IN\_BLANK/MATCHING), JSON question data (options and correct answers). |
| 25 | Quiz Question | Ordered link between a quiz and a bank question. |
| 26 | Quiz Session | One attempt: quiz, user, time limit, start/end time, score (number of correct answers). |
| 27 | Quiz Answer Detail | Answer given to one question in a session with correctness and score earned. |
| 28 | Question Report | Report on a question by a Customer, School Student or Teacher; resolved by Content Admin. |
| 29 | Quiz Rating | Rating of a quiz by a user. |
| 30 | Assignment | Homework for one class: teacher, title, description, type (CONTEXT\_READING/AI\_CHAT\_ROLEPLAY/QUIZ\_TEST), target id, minimum requirement, deadline, status (ACTIVE/CANCELLED). |
| 31 | Assignment Submission | A student's work on an assignment: status (BR-24), score, message count, reading duration, start/submit time, linked quiz session or chat session. |

### **3.2 Authentication & Account**

#### ***3.2.1 Log In***

* **Function trigger:** User opens S-02 from S-01 or any protected URL; clicks "Đăng nhập" or "Tiếp tục với Google".  
* **Function description:** All roles sign in with email and password; any user may also sign in with Google. The system returns a JWT access token and refresh token and the client routes by role: Customer/Student → S-07, Teacher → S-27, School Admin → S-36, Content Admin → S-46, System Admin → S-54. (UC-01)  
* **Screen layout:**

**![][image17]**

* **Function details:**  
  * *Data:* email (valid format), password.  
  * *Validation:* both fields required (MSG02); email format (MSG16).  
  * *Business rules:* BR-02, BR-03, BR-05, BR-06, BR-13.  
  * *Normal flow:* 1\) User enters credentials. 2\) System finds the user by email (case-insensitive), checks the BCrypt hash and that the account is not deactivated or deleted. 3\) System issues an access token and a refresh token (BR-03). 4\) If mustChangePassword is true the client opens S-05 with MSG21; otherwise the role home screen.  
  * *Google flow:* 1\) User selects a Google account. 2\) System verifies the Google ID token. 3a) Email exists → sign in with that account's role. 3b) Email is new → create a CUSTOMER account on the Free tier with a random temporary password sent by email, then sign in.  
  * *Refresh:* the client exchanges the refresh token for a new access token; a revoked or expired refresh token → MSG09.  
  * *Abnormal:* wrong email or password → MSG09 (does not reveal which one); deactivated account → MSG15; school subscription expired, suspended or not started (school roles) → MSG23; Google verification failure → MSG14.

#### ***3.2.2 Register Account***

* **Function trigger:** Visitor clicks "Đăng ký ngay" on S-01/S-02 and opens S-03.  
* **Function description:** Creates a Customer account on the Free tier. (UC-02)  
* **Screen layout:**

**![][image18]**

* **Function details:**  
  * *Validation:* all fields required (MSG02); username 3–50 characters (MSG08); valid email (MSG16); password at least 8 characters (MSG17, BR-02); confirmation matches (MSG18).  
  * *Normal flow:* system creates the user with role CUSTOMER, a Free user-tier record and a token balance equal to the Free tier's token amount (BR-08), then shows MSG04 and opens S-02.  
  * *Abnormal:* email already used → MSG19; username already used → MSG31.

#### ***3.2.3 Reset Password*** {#3.2.3-reset-password}

* **Function trigger:** User clicks "Quên mật khẩu?" on S-02 (S-04 step 1\) or opens the link in the email (S-04 step 2).  
* **Function description:** Sends a one-time reset link to the account's email; the user sets a new password from that link. (UC-03)  
* **Screen layout:**

**![][image19]**

* **Function details:**  
  * *Rules:* BR-04. Students whose account uses a generated shadow email cannot receive the email; their password is reset by the School Admin (3.10.4).  
  * *Normal flow:* 1\) System always shows MSG05 (whether or not the email exists). 2\) If the email exists, a random token is generated, its SHA-256 hash and expiry (15 minutes) are stored and the link is emailed. 3\) User submits the new password; the token is cleared and MSG03 is shown on S-02.  
  * *Abnormal:* link invalid, used or expired → MSG20; new password missing → MSG02; confirmation differs → MSG18; new password shorter than 6 characters → MSG17.

#### ***3.2.4 Change Password*** {#3.2.4-change-password}

* **Function trigger:** User opens S-05 from S-06, or is redirected there at first login.  
* **Function description:** Changes the password of the signed-in user. (UC-04)  
* **Screen layout:**

![][image20]

* **Function details:** current password must be correct (MSG09); new password 6–100 characters (MSG17); confirmation must match (MSG18). On success mustChangePassword is cleared and MSG03 is shown.

#### ***3.2.5 Update Profile, Log Out and Deactivate Own Account*** {#3.2.5-update-profile,-log-out-and-deactivate-own-account}

* **Function trigger:** User opens S-06 from the avatar menu; selects "Đăng xuất" or "Vô hiệu hóa tài khoản".  
* **Function description:** Updates profile and avatar; ends the session; deactivates the own account. (UC-05, UC-06, UC-07)  
* **Screen layout:**

**![][image21]**

* **Function details:** username, role and school are read-only. Phone must be a valid Vietnamese mobile number (MSG08). Avatar must be an image of at most 5 MB (MSG26); it is stored in Supabase Storage and shown via a signed URL. Success → MSG03. Log out adds the session token to the revocation list (BR-03) and returns to S-01. Deactivating the own account requires confirmation (MSG29), sets the account to DEACTIVATED and signs the user out.

### **3.4 AI Character Chat** {#3.4-ai-character-chat}

#### ***3.4.1 Chat with Historical Character*** {#3.4.1-chat-with-historical-character}

* **Function trigger:** User clicks "Trò chuyện" on S-11, S-15 or S-22, or resumes a session from S-14; then sends a question.  
* **Function description:** The character answers in the first person, grounded in retrieved document passages; the answer is streamed. (UC-11)  
* **Screen layout:**

**![][image25]**

* **Function details:**  
  * *Validation:* message required (MSG02), at most 4,000 characters (MSG08).  
  * *Business rules:* BR-06, BR-08 – BR-11, BR-13, BR-17, BR-18.  
  * *Normal flow:* 1\) System checks tokens: Customer balance \> 0 after the daily allowance (3.4.5); School Student/Teacher via 3.4.4. 2\) User message is saved and sent to the AI service (3.4.3). 3\) Answer is displayed progressively, followed by suggested questions and quotes. 4\) Remaining tokens are updated from the final SSE event.  
  * *Abnormal:* Customer balance 0 → S-13 with MSG10; student/teacher daily limit or school pool exhausted → S-13 with MSG22; school subscription invalid → MSG23; AI service error or timeout → MSG14, no tokens are deducted.  
  * *Out-of-scope or unsafe question:* the character politely declines in persona (BR-18).

#### 

#### ***3.4.2 View Chat History*** {#3.4.2-view-chat-history}

* **Function trigger:** User opens S-14.  
* **Function description:** Lists the user's own sessions; opens or deletes one. (UC-12)  
* **Screen layout:**

**![][image26]**

* **Function details:** opening a session loads its messages in S-12 and allows continuing; "Xóa" asks for confirmation (MSG29) and soft-deletes the session (MSG06); no sessions → MSG01.

#### ***3.4.3 AI Answer Streaming & Token Deduction (non-screen)*** {#3.4.3-ai-answer-streaming-&-token-deduction-(non-screen)}

* **Function trigger:** Each message sent from S-12 (POST /api/v1/chat/messages/stream, or /messages without streaming).  
* **Actor:** System (Java core \+ AI Service), triggered by a chat message from a Customer, School Student, Teacher or Content Admin.  
* **Function description:** Produces a grounded answer and charges tokens.  
* **Screen layout:** N/A – non-screen function.  
* **Function details:**  
  1. The Java core sends the character/context persona, the last 4 messages of the session and the question to the AI service.  
  2. The AI service embeds the question, retrieves the 10 most similar chunks of the related documents (match\_history\_chunks), re-ranks them with a cross-encoder (falls back to the top 2 chunks if the re-ranker fails) and builds the prompt.  
  3. The LLM answer is streamed back and relayed to the browser as SSE events; the last event contains prompt/completion token counts.  
  4. On completion the user and AI messages are saved with token counts, suggested questions and quotes; cost \= prompt \+ completion tokens (BR-08). Customer: balance is reduced (not below 0). School Student/Teacher: daily used tokens increase and the school pool decreases (BR-10).  
  5. If the stream fails, no cost is charged and MSG14 is returned.

#### ***3.4.4 Daily Allowance Preparation (non-screen)*** {#3.4.4-daily-allowance-preparation-(non-screen)}

* **Function trigger:** Before each chat turn of a School Student or Teacher.  
* **Actor:** System, before each chat turn of a School Student or Teacher.  
* **Function description:** Lazily resets daily counters and computes today's available tokens.  
* **Screen layout:** N/A – non-screen function.  
* **Function details:** 1\) Reject if the account is deactivated or the school subscription is invalid (BR-13). 2\) If the last reset was before today: daily used \= 0, daily bonus \= 0\. 3\) Daily limit \= teacher default (teachers) or the first active class quota, else the school default student quota (students) (BR-09). 4\) Available \= min(limit \+ bonus − used, school pool). 5\) Available ≤ 0 → MSG22.

#### ***3.4.5 Customer Daily Token Allowance (non-screen)*** {#3.4.5-customer-daily-token-allowance-(non-screen)}

* **Function trigger:** First sign-in or first chat of a Customer on a new day (UTC+7).  
* **Actor:** System, on the Customer's first sign-in or chat of the day.  
* **Function description:** Grants the daily token allowance of the Customer's active tier lazily (Issue 5).  
* **Screen layout:** N/A – non-screen function.  
* **Function details:** 1\) If the last grant was before today, the system adds the daily token amount of the Customer's active tier (Free, Plus or Pro) to the token balance; days without sign-in or chat are not granted. 2\) The daily token amount of each tier is configured by the System Admin (3.12.4) and applies from the next grant. 3\) Unused tokens are carried over and accumulate in the balance; tokens from purchases and daily quests are never removed (BR-12). 4\) The last grant time is set to now and the new balance is shown in the token badge.

### **3.5 Quiz** {#3.5-quiz}

#### ***3.5.1 Take Quiz*** {#3.5.1-take-quiz}

* **Function trigger:** User clicks "Làm bài" on S-16, S-09 or S-22 and opens S-17.  
* **Function description:** Quiz with multiple-choice, fill-in-blank and matching questions graded by the server. (UC-13)  
* **Screen layout:**

**![][image27]**

* **Function details:**  
  * *Business rules:* BR-20, BR-21, BR-23.  
  * *Normal flow:* 1\) "Bắt đầu" creates a quiz session with start time and the time limit chosen by the user before starting, if any (shown as a countdown; a quiz can also be taken without a time limit); questions are sent without answer keys. 2\) User answers and clicks "Nộp bài"; a confirmation shows the number of unanswered questions. 3\) Server grades each answer (BR-20), saves answer details, sets end time and score, and opens S-18 with MSG13. Completing a quiz counts toward the QUIZ daily quest.  
  * *Abnormal:* session already submitted → MSG28; quiz not found or unpublished → MSG32; time limit reached → the quiz can no longer be submitted and a late submission is rejected (MSG43).

#### ***3.5.2 View Quiz Result, Rate Quiz and Report Question*** {#3.5.2-view-quiz-result,-rate-quiz-and-report-question}

* **Function description:** Shows the result; lets the Customer, School Student or Teacher rate the quiz and report a question. (UC-14, UC-15)  
* **Screen layout:**

**![][image28]**

* **Function details:** score shown as correct/total and percentage; correct answers and explanations are shown after submission only (BR-21). Each user has one rating per quiz and can view or update it. A question report is sent with a reason and appears in S-50. S-19 lists own sessions newest first with paging; no sessions → MSG01.

### **3.8 Subscription & Payment** {#3.8-subscription-&-payment}

#### ***3.8.1 Purchase Subscription Package*** {#3.8.1-purchase-subscription-package}

* **Function trigger:** Customer clicks "Thanh toán ngay" on a tier in S-24.  
* **Function description:** Creates a PayOS payment order, shows VietQR and grants the tier after the verified webhook. (UC-21)  
* **Screen layout:**

![][image34]

* **Function details:**  
  * *Business rules:* BR-26 – BR-30.  
  * *Normal flow:* 1\) System checks that the customer has no active paid subscription (BR-29), creates a PENDING order with a unique order code, transfer content "HISTALK" \+ last 6 digits and an expiry of 15 minutes, and requests a PayOS payment link. 2\) S-25 shows the QR code and countdown and polls the order status. 3\) When the webhook marks the order PAID (3.8.3), fulfillment grants the tier and tokens; the popup shows MSG24.  
  * *Abnormal:* active paid subscription → MSG30; PayOS unavailable → MSG14, no order; user cancels → CANCELLED; countdown ends → EXPIRED (MSG25). The PayOS return URL only reports the client-side result; the order is completed only by the verified webhook.

#### ***3.8.2 View Payment History*** {#3.8.2-view-payment-history}

* **Function trigger:** Customer opens S-26.  
* **Function description:** Lists the customer's own orders. (UC-22)  
* **Screen layout:**

**![][image35]**

* **Function details:** read-only; shows order code, tier, amount, status (BR-26), created and expiry time; no orders → MSG01.

#### ***3.8.3 Payment Webhook Handler (non-screen)*** {#3.8.3-payment-webhook-handler-(non-screen)}

* **Function trigger:** PayOS calls POST /api/v1/payments/payos/webhook.  
* **Actor:** PayOS Gateway (webhook).  
* **Function description:** Confirms payments reliably.  
* **Screen layout:** N/A – non-screen function.  
* **Function details:** 1\) Verify the signature with the PayOS SDK and checksum key (BR-27); invalid → rejected, no change. 2\) Find the order by order code and validate the data (amount, order) against it. 3\) Only a PENDING order changes status: success code → PAID, otherwise CANCELLED/FAILED. 4\) For a PAID order, fulfillment creates an active user tier (start \= now, end \= now \+ tier months), adds the tier's token amount to the balance and marks fulfillment FULFILLED; on error fulfillment is FAILED and retried by 3.8.4. Repeated notifications have no further effect.

#### ***3.8.4 Payment Expiry, Subscription Expiry and Fulfillment Reconciliation Jobs (non-screen)*** {#3.8.4-payment-expiry,-subscription-expiry-and-fulfillment-reconciliation-jobs-(non-screen)}

* **Function trigger:** Scheduled with fixed delay: order expiry every 60 s; subscription expiry every 5 min; fulfillment reconciliation every 60 s.  
* **Actor:** System scheduler.  
* **Function description:** Keeps orders and subscriptions consistent.  
* **Screen layout:** N/A – non-screen function.  
* **Function details:** order expiry: PENDING orders with expiredAt \< now → EXPIRED. Subscription expiry: active paid user tiers with endTime \< now → inactive; the user falls back to the Free tier record (Free never expires); tokens already granted remain. Reconciliation: PAID orders whose fulfillment is PENDING/FAILED are fulfilled again (idempotent, no double grant).

## **4\. Non-Functional Requirements** {#4.-non-functional-requirements}

### **4.1 External Interfaces** {#4.1-external-interfaces}

#### ***4.1.1 User Interfaces*** {#4.1.1-user-interfaces}

* UI-01: Web application supports the latest two versions of Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari.  
* UI-02: Layout supports desktop (≥ 1366×768) and tablet (≥ 768 px); Customer and School Student screens S-07 – S-23 are also usable on phones (≥ 360 px).  
* UI-03: All UI text is Vietnamese; dates dd/MM/yyyy HH:mm (UTC+7); money with Vietnamese separators (e.g., 99.000 VNĐ).  
* UI-04: Light and dark themes; text contrast meets WCAG 2.1 AA.

#### ***4.1.2 Software Interfaces*** {#4.1.2-software-interfaces}

| Interface | Purpose | Requirement |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| PayOS API & webhook (payos-java SDK) | Create payment links, receive payment results | Webhook signature verified with the checksum key (BR-27); order query by order code. |
| AI Service (FastAPI, port 8001\) | Answer generation, document indexing | HTTP/streaming; returns prompt and completion token counts. |
| LLM provider (Ollama or OpenAI-compatible API) and re-ranker | Generation, embeddings, re-ranking | Configurable by environment; embedding dimension fixed per configured model. |
| Google Identity | Google sign-in | ID token verified server-side. |
| Email (SMTP, Spring Mail) | Password reset, temporary passwords | Sent after the transaction commits. |
| Supabase Storage | Avatars, media, map images, PDFs | Private bucket; upload links valid 300 s, view links 3,600 s. |
| PostgreSQL \+ pgvector (Supabase) | Business data and embeddings | Schema historical\_schema, versioned by Flyway. |
| Prometheus / Grafana | Monitoring | Metrics exposed at /actuator/prometheus. |

#### ***4.1.3 Hardware Interfaces*** {#4.1.3-hardware-interfaces}

No dedicated hardware interface; the system runs on standard servers/containers and is used from standard browsers.

#### ***4.1.4 Communications Interfaces*** {#4.1.4-communications-interfaces}

* COMM-01: All external traffic uses HTTPS (TLS 1.2 or higher).  
* COMM-02: AI answers and PDF extraction progress are streamed with Server-Sent Events (text/event-stream).  
* COMM-03: Client–server APIs are RESTful JSON under /api/v1, authenticated with Authorization: Bearer \<JWT\>; the contract is published with OpenAPI (Swagger UI).

### **4.2 Quality Attributes** {#4.2-quality-attributes}

#### ***4.2.1 Usability***  {#4.2.1-usability}

* USA-01: A first-time Customer can register, open a character and send the first question within 3 minutes without help.  
* USA-02: A first-time Teacher can create an assignment within 5 minutes after a 15-minute introduction (power user: within 2 minutes).  
* USA-03: A School Admin can import 500 students from the template within 10 minutes including preparing the file.  
* USA-04: Every input has a visible label; validation errors appear in red under the field (MSG02, MSG08…); destructive actions require confirmation (MSG29).  
* USA-05: Every list screen offers search/filter and paging (COM-02); empty results show MSG01.

#### ***4.2.2 Reliability***  {#4.2.2-reliability}

* REL-01 Availability: ≥ 99.5% during 06:00–23:00 (UTC+7), measured monthly, excluding announced maintenance (max 4 h/month, outside 06:00–23:00).  
* REL-02 MTBF: ≥ 720 hours for the core backend.  
* REL-03 MTTR: ≤ 30 minutes for a crashed core service (container restart policy and redeploy).  
* REL-04 Degraded mode: if the AI service is unavailable, chat returns MSG14 while all other functions keep working; if PayOS is unavailable, purchases are disabled and existing subscriptions are unaffected; if the re-ranker fails, retrieval falls back to the top 2 chunks.  
* REL-05 Data durability: daily database backups kept 30 days; RPO ≤ 24 h, RTO ≤ 4 h.  
* REL-06 Accuracy: quiz grading is deterministic on the server (BR-20); assignment scores are rounded to 2 decimals (BR-22); a token deduction always equals the token usage reported by the AI service (BR-08).  
* REL-07 AI grounding: in an acceptance test of 100 questions per sampled character, ≥ 90% of answers contain only facts supported by the retrieved passages.  
* REL-08 OCR accuracy: ≥ 85% character accuracy on clear printed Vietnamese scans at 300 dpi.  
* REL-09 Defect rate, by category:  
  * **Critical** – data loss or corruption, cross-school data leak (BR-01), payment accepted without the tier/tokens granted, wrong quiz/assignment score, or a main use case (UC-01, UC-11, UC-13, UC-19, UC-21, UC-23, UC-29) blocked with no workaround. Target: 0 open critical defects at each milestone; ≤ 0.5 critical defects/KLOC found in test.  
  * **Significant** – a function works incorrectly but a workaround exists. Target ≤ 1 defect/KLOC; fixed within 24 h.  
  * **Minor** – cosmetic or text issues that do not affect function. Target ≤ 2 defects/KLOC; fixed in the next release.

#### ***4.2.3 Performance*** {#4.2.3-performance}

* PER-01 AI response (UC-11): first part of the answer displayed within 1.5 s for 95% of questions (TTFT); complete answer within 15 s for 95% of questions.  
* PER-02 Response time: non-AI requests average ≤ 200 ms, 95% ≤ 300 ms, maximum 1 s under normal load.  
* PER-03 Throughput: at least 50 non-AI requests per second sustained.  
* PER-04 Capacity: 500 concurrent active users and 100 concurrent AI chat streams without breaching PER-01/PER-02.  
* PER-05 Batch: a CSV import of 1,000 students (UC-29) completes within 60 s; a 100-page text PDF is extracted within 2 minutes and a 100-page scan within 20 minutes (UC-40).  
* PER-06 Resource utilization: under the PER-04 load, CPU ≤ 70% and memory ≤ 75% on each application server; database connections ≤ 80% of the pool.

#### ***4.2.4 Security***

* SEC-01 Tenant isolation: every query on school data is filtered by the user's school; no API returns another school's data (BR-01).  
* SEC-02 Authentication: passwords stored with BCrypt; JWT signed with HMAC-SHA256; reset tokens stored only as SHA-256 hashes (BR-04).  
* SEC-03 Authorization: every API checks the role (@PreAuthorize) and the data scope of section 3.1.3 on the server side; unauthorized requests return HTTP 403 (MSG11).  
* SEC-04 Quiz integrity: answer keys are never sent to the client before submission (BR-21).  
* SEC-05 Payment: webhook signatures verified (BR-27); no card or bank data is stored by HistoryTalk.  
* SEC-06 AI safety: characters resist instructions that try to change their persona or reveal system instructions (BR-18); user input is never executed or rendered as HTML.  
* SEC-07 Personal data: only data needed for the service is collected; students' data is visible only to their school staff; handling follows Vietnam's personal data protection regulations.  
* SEC-08 Files: storage is private; files are accessed only through time-limited signed URLs.

#### ***4.2.5 Maintainability*** {#4.2.5-maintainability}

* MAI-01 The core backend and the AI service are deployed independently.  
* MAI-02 Every database schema change is applied through versioned Flyway migrations; version numbers must be unique.  
* MAI-03 Tier prices and tokens, school quotas, password-reset expiry, storage URL expiry and JWT lifetimes are configurable without code changes.  
* MAI-04 Unit test coverage ≥ 70% for business rules BR-08 – BR-12, BR-14, BR-20 – BR-24, BR-26 – BR-30. Measured with JaCoCo line coverage on the classes implementing these rules (mvn verify).

## **5\. Requirement Appendix**

### **5.1 Business Rules** {#5.1-business-rules}

| ID | Rule Definition |
| ----- | ----- |
| **Tenant, accounts & sessions** |  |
| BR-01 | Tenant isolation: School Admins, Teachers and Students can only view and change data of their own school. Global content is visible to everyone; local content only inside its school (BR-16). |
| BR-02 | Passwords: registration requires at least 8 characters; changed or reset passwords require 6–100 characters; confirmation must match. |
| BR-03 | Sessions use a JWT access token (default lifetime 24 h, configurable) and a refresh token (configurable). Logging out revokes the presented token; a revoked refresh token cannot be used. |
| BR-04 | A password reset link is valid for 15 minutes (configurable) and can be used once; requesting a new link replaces the previous one. The response never reveals whether the email exists. |
| BR-05 | Usernames: students {school\_code}\_hs\_{student\_code}, teachers {school\_code}\_gv\_…, School Admins {school\_code}\_admin, all lower case, with a numeric suffix if already taken. Issued accounts must change password at first login. |
| BR-06 | A DEACTIVATED or deleted account cannot sign in or use AI chat. |
| BR-07 | A Teacher can only manage classes, assignments, analytics and token requests of classes where he/she is the homeroom teacher. |
| **Token economy** |  |
| BR-08 | Token cost of one chat turn \= prompt tokens \+ completion tokens reported by the AI service. Failed answers are not charged. A Customer starts with the Free tier's token amount and can chat while the balance is greater than 0; the balance never becomes negative. |
| BR-09 | Daily limit of a School Student \= quota of his/her active class if set, otherwise the school default (default 1,000). Daily limit of a Teacher \= school teacher default (default 10,000). Counters reset lazily on the first chat of a new day; unused tokens are not carried over. |
| BR-10 | All tokens used by students and teachers are deducted from the school pool. Available today \= min(daily limit \+ daily bonus − used today, school pool). When the pool is 0, chat is blocked for the whole school (MSG22). |
| BR-11 | Extra tokens: a student may send one PENDING request per day to the homeroom teacher. The teacher can approve (transfer from the teacher's remaining daily allowance to the student's daily bonus), reject or escalate to the School Admin. The School Admin approves from the school pool. Bonus tokens are valid only for the current day. |
| BR-12 | Daily quest rewards, the daily allowance of the active tier (3.4.5) and paid tiers add tokens to a Customer's balance; tokens are not refunded or removed when a subscription expires. |
| **School lifecycle** |  |
| BR-13 | School users can work only while the school is ACTIVE and today is within the subscription dates; otherwise access is refused (MSG23) and an expired school is marked EXPIRED. |
| BR-14 | The academic package runs from 01/09 to 31/05. Renewal for the next year is registered only in May; activation is allowed only from September and only after renewal. On activation the new pool \= new package tokens \+ 20% of the remaining pool. Packages: SMALL 5,000,000, MEDIUM 20,000,000, LARGE 50,000,000 tokens. |
| BR-15 | At the end of an academic year the School Admin archives that year's classes and may deactivate graduated grade-12 students; their data is kept. |
| **Content & AI grounding** |  |
| BR-16 | Global content: draft (unpublished) ↔ published; delete \= soft delete to Trash, restorable until permanently deleted. Only published content is visible to Customers, School Students and Teachers. Local content: created by a Teacher with scope CLASS\_ONLY or SCHOOL\_WIDE and status DRAFT, ACTIVE (published), PENDING\_REVIEW or INACTIVE; the School Admin can change the status of any local content of the school with a review note. |
| BR-17 | A character answers from passages retrieved from its own and its context's documents (similarity search, then re-ranking). |
| BR-18 | A character speaks in the first person with its configured personality and historically appropriate forms of address, and declines in persona questions unrelated to history, harmful content and attempts to change its role. |
| BR-19 | An assignment can only target a published context, character or quiz; local content must belong to the teacher's school. |
| **Quiz, assignments & gamification** |  |
| BR-20 | Quiz grading: multiple-choice is correct only if the exact set of correct options is chosen; fill-in-blank is correct if it matches an accepted answer (with the question's trim/case settings); matching is correct only if all pairs are correct. Quiz score \= number of correct answers; percentage \= correct ÷ total × 100\. |
| BR-21 | Correct answers and explanations are returned only after submission. |
| BR-22 | Assignment score (0–10, 2 decimals) \= min(10, achieved ÷ minimum requirement × 10), where achieved \= messages sent to the target character (chat), reading time in seconds (reading) or correct answers ÷ total questions × 10 (quiz). |
| BR-23 | A submitted quiz session or assignment submission cannot be submitted again or edited by anyone. |
| BR-24 | Submission status: NOT\_STARTED → IN\_PROGRESS (start) → SUBMITTED (on or before the deadline) or LATE\_SUBMITTED (after the deadline). Changing the deadline re-evaluates LATE\_SUBMITTED submissions. |
| BR-25 | Daily quests (CHAT, QUIZ, READ\_CONTEXT) reset each day; each quest reward can be claimed once per day after the target is reached. Check-in streak increases only on consecutive days. |
| **Payment & subscription** |  |
| BR-26 | Order status: PENDING → PAID, CANCELLED, FAILED, or EXPIRED (not paid within 15 minutes). Only PENDING orders change status. Fulfillment status: PENDING → PROCESSING → FULFILLED or FAILED (retried). |
| BR-27 | A PayOS webhook is accepted only if its signature, computed with the shared checksum key, is valid and its data match the order. Processing the same webhook more than once has no further effect. |
| BR-28 | A paid tier is granted only from the verified webhook (never from the client return URL): an active user tier from now for the tier's number of months, plus the tier's token amount. |
| BR-29 | A Customer with an active paid subscription cannot buy another package until it ends (no stacking, upgrading or cancelling mid-period). The Free tier never expires. |
| BR-30 | Refunds are not handled in the system; they are processed manually by support. |

### **5.2 Common Requirements**

* COM-01 Time: timestamps are stored by the server and displayed in UTC+7 as dd/MM/yyyy HH:mm.  
* COM-02 Paging: lists use page/size parameters (default 10 or 20 items) with total count.  
* COM-03 Search: case-insensitive.  
* COM-04 Text fields are trimmed; required fields are marked with \*; maximum lengths enforced with MSG08.  
* COM-05 Deletion: content and accounts are soft-deleted (deleted\_at); content can be restored from Trash or permanently deleted by an authorized user; there is no automatic purge.  
* COM-06 Every API response uses the common envelope (success flag, message, data, pagination metadata) and validation errors list each invalid field.  
* COM-07 Every successful create/update/trash/restore action shows MSG04, MSG03, MSG06 or MSG07.  
* COM-08 Emails are sent only after the database transaction commits.

### **5.4 Other Requirements** {#5.4-other-requirements}

# **IV. Software Design Description**

This section presents the comprehensive architectural and detailed software design specifications for the HistoryTalk platform, incorporating the audited Review 2 guidelines, updated multi-tiered infrastructure, data models, class contracts, and core business workflows.

## **1\. System Design**

### **1.1 System Architecture**

HistoryTalk is a modular educational platform serving both B2B Educational Institutions (Multi-tenant Schools, Classrooms, Teachers, and School Students) and B2C Self-Directed Learners (Customers). The system separates transactional business operations, access control, and institutional lifecycle management from compute-intensive Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), vector similarity search, cross-encoder reranking, and streaming Large Language Model (LLM) roleplay inference

![][image69]

***Figure 1: HistoryTalk System Architecture Overview***

The system architecture comprises four primary architectural tiers, an edge reverse proxy, and external service integrations:

3. **1\. Client Tier:** Client web application built with Next.js, React, and Tailwind CSS. It provides role-tailored workspaces for platform actors (Customer, School Student, Teacher, School Admin, Content Admin, and System Admin), interactive spatio-temporal historical maps with GeoJSON movement paths, 3D historical character models (.glb), Server-Sent Events (SSE) streaming roleplay chat, and gradebook management. A mobile app prototype based on React Native/Expo is scheduled for the product roadmap (not included in Release 1.0).  
4. **2\. Caddy Reverse Proxy:** Positioned between client traffic and backend services to handle automatic TLS termination, request rate limiting, static asset compression, and clean API routing. Caddy routes all public '/api/\*' requests directly to the Java Core Backend while serving frontend assets securely.  
5. **3\. Core Backend Application:** Java 21 / Spring Boot central application handling all core business rules, entity transactions, security filters (JwtAuthenticationFilter), school subscription lifecycle guards (SchoolSubscriptionGuardInterceptor), multi-tenant data isolation by school\_id, digital PDF extraction (Apache PDFBox) and scanned document OCR (Tess4J), and PayOS payment webhooks. The Node.js real-time/proxy component originally considered in preliminary drafts was superseded by direct SSE relaying across the Java core and FastAPI service, eliminating unnecessary inter-process hops.  
6. **4\. AI & Hybrid RAG Engine:** Dedicated Python FastAPI service exposing asynchronous endpoints. It executes dynamic semantic chunking, generates multilingual dense embeddings (BAAI/bge-m3), queries Supabase PgVector for candidate passages, coordinates reranking via the Cross-Encoder Reranker service (HTTP /api/rerank, configured via RERANKER\_URL), and streams grounded first-person historical persona dialogues with Socratic reverse-questioning.  
7. **5\. Data Persistence & Vector Storage Tier:** Combines PostgreSQL (local postgres:15-alpine for development; managed Supabase PostgreSQL in production) housing relational tables in historical\_schema, along with the Supabase PgVector extension storing vector\_chunk data indexed with HNSW cosine distance.  
8. **6\. External Third-Party Integrations:** Integrates Google OAuth 2.0 (SSO login), Supabase Storage (storage of PDFs, 2D avatar images, 3D GLB character models, and map rasters via signed URLs), PayOS Payment Gateway (VietQR checkout and webhook verification), SMTP Mail Server (transactional emails), Ollama / OpenAI-compatible LLM host, Cross-Encoder Reranker service, and Prometheus/Grafana monitoring.

### **1.2 Package Diagram**

#### ***1.2.1 Core Backend Packages (Java Spring Boot)***

The Java backend follows a strict layered and domain-partitioned package organization under 'com.historytalk', ensuring clean separation between HTTP presentation, security filters, domain business logic, and JPA persistence.

***![][image70]*** 

***Figure 2: Package Diagram \-- Core Backend Service (com.historytalk)***

| No | Package Name | Layer / Responsibility Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 01 | com.historytalk.config | Configures Spring Security filter chains (SecurityConfig), OpenAPI documentation (OpenApiConfig), PayOS SDK client (PayOSConfig), OAuth2 properties, and MVC interceptors. |
| 02 | com.historytalk.security | Implements JWT token parsing, verification, and revocation checks (JwtAuthenticationFilter, JwtTokenProvider), B2B school subscription guards (SchoolSubscriptionGuardInterceptor), and Google OAuth2 handlers. |
| 03 | com.historytalk.controller.\* | Exposes RESTful API controllers grouped into domain subpackages: authentication, user, school, classroom, assignment, historicalContext, character, localContent, document, map, chat, quiz, gamification, payment, dashboard, and trash. |
| 04 | com.historytalk.dto.\* | Encapsulates strongly-typed Request and Response Data Transfer Objects across domain subpackages, along with standardized envelope wrappers (ApiResponse, PaginatedApiResponse, ValidationErrorResponse). |
| 05 | com.historytalk.service.\* | Implements and executes domain business logic: user account management, CSV student bulk roster enrollment, daily token quota and ticket boost workflows, PDF/OCR processing, quiz auto-grading, and resilient PayOS fulfillment. |
| 06 | com.historytalk.mapper.\* | Maps internal JPA domain entities to external DTO contracts (CharacterMapper, UserMapper, PaymentMapper, TierMapper) preventing persistence internals from leaking. |
| 07 | com.historytalk.repository.\* | Defines Spring Data JPA repository interfaces and analytical projection query interfaces (repository.dashboard) for system, school, and classroom analytics. |
| 08 | com.historytalk.entity.\* | Contains persistent JPA domain entities across domain subpackages and domain enumerations (entity.enums). |
| 09 | com.historytalk.exception | Centralizes exception handling via GlobalExceptionHandler and domain exception hierarchy (ResourceNotFoundException, InvalidRequestException, DataConflictException, ForbiddenException). |
| 10 | com.historytalk.utils | Provides security context helpers (SecurityUtils) and UUID validation/conversion utilities (UuidUtils). |

#### ***1.2.2 AI & RAG Engine Packages (Python FastAPI)***

The Python AI service is organized under 'src/history\_talk\_ai' following a four-layer architecture (presentation, application, dataaccess, and common).

***![][image71]*** 

***Figure 3: Package Diagram \-- AI & RAG Engine (history\_talk\_ai)***

| No | Package Name | Layer / Responsibility Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 01 | presentation.chat.router | Exposes FastAPI endpoints under /v1/ai: POST /chat, POST /chat/stream, POST /generate-title, POST /documents/process, DELETE /documents/{doc\_id}, GET /character/{character\_id}, GET /context/{context\_id} secured by internal API key validation. |
| 02 | presentation.chat.schemas | Defines Pydantic request and response models (GenerateReplyRequest, GenerateReplyResponse, MessageHistoryItem, ProcessDocumentRequest, GenerateTitleRequest). |
| 03 | application.chat.service | Implements the core RAG and LLM pipeline: dynamic semantic chunking (\_semantic\_chunking), BGE-M3 embedding generation (get\_embedding\_from\_ollama), Supabase vector retrieval, reranking via RERANKER\_URL, and SSE streaming roleplay. |
| 04 | application.prompting | Contains prompt\_builder.py, constructing first-person historical persona instructions, anti-hallucination constraints, and Socratic questioning directives. |
| 05 | dataaccess.java\_backend | Implements asynchronous http client (client.py) and typed schemas (character\_schema.py, historical\_context\_schema.py) to fetch character biographies and context metadata from the Java Core Backend. |
| 06 | common.config | Manages environment configuration via pydantic-settings (settings.py), binding LLM provider routing (ollama vs. external API), model parameters, Supabase credentials, and timeout thresholds. |
| 07 | common.errors | Provides global FastAPI exception handlers and structured JSON error responses for upstream timeouts, embedding errors, or LLM inference failures. |

## **2\. Database Design**

### **2.1 Entity-Relationship Diagram**

HistoryTalk uses PostgreSQL (historical\_schema) for relations, Supabase PgVector (public) for embeddings, and Flyway for version control, combining relational tables, link tables, and vector\_chunk queried via match\_history\_chunks

***![][image73]***

***Figure 5: Complete Entity-Relationship Diagram (ERD across all Bounded Domains)***

### **2.2 Database Table Descriptions**

Table below summarizes the database tables in HistoryTalk, specifying the business purpose, Primary Keys (PK), and Foreign Keys (FK) in alignment with JPA entity models and database migrations:

| No | Table Name | Primary Keys (PK), Foreign Keys (FK) & Purpose Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 01 | school | Stores B2B multi-tenant school organizations, enterprise subscription packages (ENTERPRISE\_SMALL, ENTERPRISE\_MEDIUM, ENTERPRISE\_LARGE), shared token pools, academic subscription dates (01/09 to 31/05), and default daily student/teacher token quotas (BR-09).• PK: id• FK: None |
| 02 | user | Stores all platform user accounts across platform roles (CUSTOMER, CONTENT\_ADMIN, SYSTEM\_ADMIN, SCHOOL\_ADMIN, TEACHER, SCHOOL\_STUDENT), credentials, account status, B2C token balance, and B2B daily token consumption.• PK: uid• FK: school\_id \-\> school(id) |
| 03 | classroom | Represents school classrooms managed by teachers for a specific grade level (6-12) and academic year, with optional per-classroom daily student token quota overrides.• PK: id• FK: school\_id \-\> school(id), teacher\_id \-\> user(uid) |
| 04 | class\_student | Junction table mapping enrolled school students to classrooms with enrollment timestamps and active/transferred status.• PK: id• FK: classroom\_id \-\> classroom(id), student\_id \-\> user(uid) |
| 05 | token\_boost\_request | Tracks token tickets submitted by students (to homeroom teachers) or teachers (to School Admins), supporting two-stage review (PENDING \-\> PENDING\_ADMIN \-\> APPROVED/REJECTED).• PK: id• FK: school\_id \-\> school(id), classroom\_id \-\> classroom(id) (nullable), student\_uid \-\> user(uid) (nullable), requester\_uid \-\> user(uid), teacher\_reviewed\_by\_uid \-\> user(uid), admin\_reviewed\_by\_uid \-\> user(uid) |
| 06 | historical\_context | Stores historical events, campaigns, eras (ANCIENT, MEDIEVAL, MODERN, CONTEMPORARY), categories, GeoJSON battle-map configurations, and multi-tenant local content states.• PK: context\_id• FK: created\_by \-\> user(uid), school\_id \-\> school(id), approved\_by \-\> user(uid) |
| 07 | character | Stores historical figure personas, biographical backgrounds, speaking styles/personalities, 2D avatars, 3D model URLs (.glb), lifespan dates, and local content states.• PK: character\_id• FK: created\_by \-\> user(uid), school\_id \-\> school(id), approved\_by \-\> user(uid) |
| 08 | context\_character\_mapping | Many-to-many bridge table associating historical characters with one or more historical contexts/campaigns.• PK: mapping\_id• FK: context\_id \-\> historical\_context(context\_id), character\_id \-\> character(character\_id) |
| 09 | class\_local\_content | Assigns school-owned local historical contexts or characters (CLASS\_ONLY or SCHOOL\_WIDE) to specific classrooms.• PK: id• FK: class\_id \-\> classroom(id), assigned\_by \-\> user(uid) |
| 10 | document | Stores reference historical documents (TEXT, MARKDOWN, PDF, IMAGE\_2D, MODEL\_3D) attached polymorphically to contexts or characters for RAG grounding.• PK: doc\_id• FK: uploaded\_by \-\> user(uid) |
| 11 | document\_media\_metadata | Polymorphic media metadata table storing Supabase Storage paths, dimensions, file sizes, and formats for characters, contexts, documents, and avatars.• PK: metadata\_id• FK: document\_id \-\> document(doc\_id) |
| 12 | vector\_chunk | Supabase PgVector table (lives in schema public) storing semantically chunked document passages and 768-D BAAI/bge-m3 dense embeddings indexed with HNSW cosine similarity, queried via RPC match\_history\_chunks.• PK: chunk\_id• FK: doc\_id, entity\_id (logical reference) |
| 13 | map\_pin | Stores interactive map markers (ADMIN or USER owned), coordinates, historical years, and GeoJSON LineString troop movement paths for a historical context.• PK: pin\_id• FK: context\_id \-\> historical\_context(context\_id), created\_by \-\> user(uid) |
| 14 | map\_focus | Stores predefined camera viewpoints (latitude, longitude, zoom level, display order) guiding learners through key geographical stages of a campaign.• PK: focus\_id• FK: context\_id \-\> historical\_context(context\_id), created\_by \-\> user(uid) |
| 15 | chat\_session | Tracks conversational AI roleplay sessions between a user and a historical character within a specific historical context.• PK: session\_id• FK: uid \-\> user(uid), context\_id \-\> historical\_context(context\_id), character\_id \-\> character(character\_id) |
| 16 | message | Stores individual user and AI dialogue turns within a chat session, including token usage, 3 AI-suggested follow-up questions, and cited RAG historical quotes.• PK: message\_id• FK: session\_id \-\> chat\_session(session\_id) |
| 17 | quiz | Stores assessment quizzes linked to historical contexts, categorized by difficulty level (EASY, MEDIUM, HARD) and publication status.• PK: quiz\_id• FK: context\_id \-\> historical\_context(context\_id), created\_by \-\> user(uid) |
| 18 | question | Central question bank supporting three polymorphic question types (MULTIPLE\_CHOICE, FILL\_IN\_BLANK, MATCHING) with JSON payload question\_data and explanations.• PK: question\_id• FK: quiz\_id \-\> quiz(quiz\_id) (nullable for bank questions) |
| 19 | quiz\_question | Many-to-many link table binding reusable Question Bank items to Quizzes with explicit order\_index and stored points weight.• PK: (quiz\_id, question\_id)• FK: quiz\_id \-\> quiz(quiz\_id), question\_id \-\> question(question\_id) |
| 20 | quiz\_session | Records a learner's timed quiz attempt, start/end timestamps, time limit, number of correct answers (score), and percentage per BR-20.• PK: session\_id• FK: quiz\_id \-\> quiz(quiz\_id), uid \-\> user(uid) |
| 21 | quiz\_answer\_detail | Stores per-question submitted answer JSON (answer\_data), correctness flag, and score\_earned (1.0 or 0.0) within a quiz attempt session.• PK: answer\_id• FK: session\_id \-\> quiz\_session(session\_id), question\_id \-\> question(question\_id) |
| 22 | quiz\_rating | Stores 1 to 5 star ratings submitted by learners after completing a quiz (enforcing one rating per user per quiz).• PK: rating\_id• FK: quiz\_id \-\> quiz(quiz\_id), user\_id \-\> user(uid) |
| 23 | question\_report | Stores learner/teacher error reports flagging factual or formatting issues on specific quiz questions for Content Admin review.• PK: report\_id• FK: question\_id \-\> question(question\_id), quiz\_id \-\> quiz(quiz\_id), reported\_by \-\> user(uid) |
| 24 | assignment | Stores classroom homework assignments created by teachers across three learning modes (CONTEXT\_READING, AI\_CHAT\_ROLEPLAY, QUIZ\_TEST) with deadlines and minimum completion thresholds.• PK: id• FK: classroom\_id \-\> classroom(id), teacher\_id \-\> user(uid) |
| 25 | assignment\_submission | Tracks individual student progress, submission status (NOT\_STARTED, IN\_PROGRESS, SUBMITTED, LATE\_SUBMITTED, MISSED, EXEMPTED), score, AI roleplay message count, and reading duration.• PK: id• FK: assignment\_id \-\> assignment(id), student\_id \-\> user(uid), quiz\_session\_id \-\> quiz\_session(session\_id), chat\_session\_id \-\> chat\_session(session\_id) |
| 26 | tier | Defines B2C subscription plans (Free, Plus, Pro), pricing in VND, billing duration in months, and token allowances.• PK: tier\_id• FK: None |
| 27 | user\_tier | Records active and historical B2C tier subscriptions for users, linking to the originating payment\_order.• PK: id• FK: uid \-\> user(uid), tier\_id \-\> tier(tier\_id), order\_id \-\> payment\_order(order\_id) |
| 28 | payment\_order | Tracks PayOS checkout orders, unique numeric order\_code, QR checkout URLs, payment status (PENDING, PAID, CANCELLED, EXPIRED, FAILED), and resilient fulfillment state (PENDING, PROCESSING, FULFILLED, FAILED).• PK: order\_id• FK: uid \-\> user(uid), tier\_id \-\> tier(tier\_id) |
| 29 | payment\_transaction | Immutable audit log of incoming PayOS webhook payloads, bank reference numbers, and verification statuses.• PK: transaction\_id• FK: order\_id \-\> payment\_order(order\_id) |
| 30 | daily\_quest | Master catalog of daily gamification quests (CHAT, QUIZ, READ\_CONTEXT), completion targets, and token rewards.• PK: quest\_id• FK: None |
| 31 | user\_quest\_progress | Tracks daily per-user progress toward active quests and reward claim status.• PK: id• FK: user\_uid \-\> user(uid), quest\_id \-\> daily\_quest(quest\_id) |
| 32 | daily\_check\_in | Records daily user login check-ins and consecutive day streak counts.• PK: id• FK: user\_uid \-\> user(uid) |

## **3\. Detailed Design**

### **3.1 Authentication, Account Lifecycle & User Access Control**

#### ***3.1.1 Class Diagram***

![][image74] 

***Figure 6: Class Diagram \-- Authentication, Account Lifecycle & Access Control***

| Class / Component | Role & Responsibility Description |
| :---- | :---- |
| AuthController | REST API controller (/api/v1/auth) handling customer registration, credential login, JWT refresh rotation, logout, and forgot/reset password endpoints. |
| AdminUserController | REST API controller (/api/v1/admin/users) for SYSTEM\_ADMIN and SCHOOL\_ADMIN to query paginated user lists, update roles, deactivate accounts, and restore soft-deleted users. |
| UserController | REST API controller (/api/v1/users) managing user profile retrieval, profile updates, and first-login mandatory password changes (mustChangePassword). |
| UserAvatarController | REST API controller (/api/v1/users/avatar) managing direct profile avatar uploads and updates in Supabase Storage using signed URLs. |
| JwtAuthenticationFilter | Spring Security OncePerRequestFilter that extracts Bearer JWT tokens, validates signature and expiry, and rejects revoked tokens or tokens of DEACTIVATED users. |
| SchoolSubscriptionGuardInterceptor | Spring MVC HandlerInterceptor enforcing B2B tenant guards: lazily checks subscription expiration and blocks requests when a school is EXPIRED or SUSPENDED. |
| AuthService / AuthServiceImpl | Core authentication service managing BCrypt password hashing, dual-token issuance, token revocation, and SHA-256 hashed password reset tokens. |
| GoogleOAuthServiceImpl | Processes Google OAuth 2.0 SSO callbacks, auto-provisions first-time CUSTOMER accounts, and dispatches credentials via GoogleOAuthPasswordEmailService. |
| JwtTokenProvider | Cryptographic utility for signing and parsing access and refresh JWTs containing uid, role, and schoolId claims. |
| UserRepository / User | Spring Data JPA repository and persistent domain entity encapsulating account credentials, roles, token balances, and audit timestamps. |

| AcademicLifecycleServiceImpl | Executes end-of-year rollover (SRS 3.10.8): archives finished classrooms, resets daily token counters, and deactivates graduating Grade 12 student accounts (reason GRADUATED). |
| StudentImportServiceImpl | Coordinates CSV bulk student account creation using Apache Commons CSV, generating temporary passwords and requiring first-login password updates. |
| DailyTokenAllowanceServiceImpl | Enforces B2B student and teacher daily token limits with lazy midnight resets, resolving effective limits from classroom overrides or school defaults (default\_daily\_teacher\_quota). |
| TokenBoostRequestServiceImpl | Manages token tickets (SRS 3.7.3, 3.9.5, 3.10.7): student requests (PENDING) are reviewed by teachers from daily allowances or escalated to School Admins (PENDING\_ADMIN) for school pool allocation. |

| JavaBackendClient (Python FastAPI) | Asynchronous http client fetching verified character biographies and historical context metadata from the Java Core Backend. |

| Class / Component | Role & Responsibility Description |
| :---- | :---- |

| PaymentFulfillmentService | Executes idempotent, pessimistic-locked order fulfillment (PENDING \-\> PROCESSING \-\> FULFILLED), activating UserTier and crediting token balances. |

## **4\. State Machine Diagrams & Main Business Workflows**

### **4.1 Entity State Machine Diagrams**

To ensure consistency between software design and business rules, the state transitions of all stateful domain entities are modeled below:

***![][image90]***

***Figure 22: State Machine Diagrams \-- ContentStatus, AccountStatus & SchoolStatus Lifecycles***

![][image91]

***Figure 23: State Machine Diagrams \-- AssignmentStatus, SubmissionStatus & TokenBoostRequestStatus***

![][image92]

***Figure 24: State Machine Diagrams \-- PaymentOrderStatus, FulfillmentStatus & PaymentTransactionStatus***

| Entity / Lifecycle | Valid States | Allowed State Transitions | Triggering Endpoint / Business Event |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
